title: Does Your Personality Affect How Well You Age?
paragraphs: What's the secret to staying healthy and happy as you age? Maybe personality?

Researchers from the University of Cagliari on the Italian island of Sardinia wanted to see how people's personalities might affect how well they age. They also wanted to see if personality differences might help explain why people in Sardinia's "Blue Zone" age better than those in other parts of the island.
Blue Zones are areas where people live unusually long and healthy lives. Sardinia's Blue Zone comprises a small number of villages in the mountains of the central-eastern part of the island.

The researchers looked at 55 people living in Sardinia's Blue Zone, and 70 living in a neighboring area — all aged between 71 and 101. Participants did tests of their personality, as well as of their psychological well-being and health-related quality of life.

People who were more responsible and organized, as well as those who were more open to new experiences, had better psychological well-being. This may be because they were better at dealing with problems and asking others for help.
However, personality had little effect on health-related quality of life.

There was also little difference in health-related quality of life between those in the Blue Zone and those in the neighboring area. But people in the Blue Zone were more open to new experiences and better at dealing with problems — and spent 66% more time on hobbies.
These hobbies may actually help support Blue Zone residents' psychological well-being.

Blue Zone residents also seemed to be conscious of how their physical limitations changed as they aged, and adapted their hobbies to match. And they may be good at making these changes because of their greater openness to new experiences and ability to deal with problems.
So your personality may not directly help you age better — but it may help you accept and adapt to your limitations, which is indeed better for you overall!
